title: EDUCATION: Beyond the Chatbot, Beyond Efficiency
author: Eric Hudson
summary: Eric Hudson argues that education's AI discourse has been trapped in two narrow frames -- the chatbot interface and efficiency metrics -- and that the last six months of AI development demand expansion beyond both. New capabilities include vibecoding (AI-assisted app development via plain English), agentic AI (autonomous multi-step task completion), and wearable AI (AI embedded in glasses and other body-worn devices). These capabilities raise questions that efficiency alone cannot answer: what are schools actually good at, and can AI make them better? What must be transformed rather than adapted? Hudson quotes Stefan Bauschard's observation that schools producing standardised minds are producing exactly the population AI substitutes for. He argues assessment must evolve beyond browser lockdown tools designed for chatbots and presents a dual-path framework: scale AI where it is effective, protect and invest in uniquely human-centered learning where it cannot be replicated.
points: The chatbot and efficiency frames are too narrow -- vibecoding, agentic AI, and wearable AI require entirely new educational frameworks.
Vibecoding democratises app development; agentic AI completes multi-step tasks autonomously; wearable AI continuously observes and captures our environment.
The factory model of education -- standardised scope, sequence, rubric, credential -- is exactly what AI is best at replacing.
Assessment tools like browser lockdowns are designed for chatbots; they are irrelevant when AI is embedded in body-worn devices.
Dual-path approach: scale AI where effective, protect and invest in human-centered approaches where AI cannot replicate them.
quotes: We have become used to talking about AI in terms of efficiency. Chatbots can produce work quickly and often competently, leading us to focus on questions of how much time AI does and does not save us.

Vibecoding with AI makes us all app developers. Agentic AI allows us to assign AI tasks to complete autonomously with minimal oversight. Wearable AI puts on our bodies AI that listens, observes, and captures our surroundings in real time.

A society that produces standardized minds -- minds shaped by the same scope and sequence, evaluated by the same rubric, certified by the same credential -- is producing exactly the population AI is best at substituting for. The factory model is not a defense against AI. The factory model is what AI is replacing.

Blue books and proctored exams and browser lockdown apps are interventions designed for chatbots. These researchers ask us to consider what assessment should look like when generative AI is on our bodies at all times.
What are we good at in schools? How can AI make us better at those things? What has AI made less effective in schools?
